title: Upper bound for infima of bounded families
statement: Let $\iota$ be a nonempty type, let $\kappa$ be a type, and let $g:\iota\to\kappa\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0\le g(i,j)\le 1$ for every $i\in\iota$ and $j\in\kappa$. Then the range of the function assigning to each $j$ the infimum of $g(i,j)$ over $i\in\iota$ is bounded above.
replaced:
Let $\iota$ be nonempty and let $g : \iota \to \kappa \to \bbr$ take values in $[0,1]$,
i.e.\ $0 \le g(i,j) \le 1$ for all $i, j$. Then the family
$j \mapsto \inf_{i \in \iota} g(i, j)$ has range bounded above.
